question: Does the 2017 Pterygoplichthys Luzon preprint provide river-specific historical evidence for the source-named Sariaya waterways?
purpose: Record historical, source-described invasive-fish leads with explicit taxonomic, date, locality, peer-review, and reuse limits.

sourceDetails.title: Invasion Status of Pterygoplichthys spp. (Pisces: Loricariidae) in the Luzon Island, Philippines and its Policy Implications
sourceDetails.pageStatus: ResearchGate labels it a preprint; early-stage research may not have been peer reviewed. The uploaded PDF states content may be subject to copyright.
sourceDetails.methodsSummary: Authors say they inspected reported localities, interviewed residents and officials, used GPS for study sites, and made photo catalogs of collected fish when samples were available. The Sariaya section does not link a specimen/voucher to either river.

localityFindings.finding: Visited several times; fishers reportedly said SACs were caught in nets. At an upstream locality residents reportedly said SACs had been in the river since 2003. No fish-specific event date or identified river voucher is linked to the catch reports.
localityFindings.coordinateHandling: The paper prints a GPS coordinate for an upstream locality; it is not adopted as river geometry or a verified taxon record.

localityFindings.place: vicinity of Maasin River Bridge, Sariaya
localityFindings.finding: Authors report seeing two SACs on the bridge footing; one resident reportedly described regular catches. The passage provides no specimen/voucher linkage, species-level determination, or event date.

taxonomicInterpretation.disposition: Retain as historical genus/group-level research leads only; do not create a species assertion.

nameCrosswalk.relationship: BMB Atlas 2016 independently lists “Malaquing Ilog River” for Sariaya, crosswalking the preprint spelling at source-name/locality level; relationship to the differently spelled Quezon profile “MalakingIlog” central river basin remains unverified.
nameCrosswalk.decision: Add the atlas spelling as an alias/source reference for the existing MalaquingIlog lead; keep the Quezon profile MalakingIlog lead separate until a direct hydrography or LGU source resolves the basin/channel and name relationship.

reuse.disposition: Do not reproduce source figures or tables or publish the interview claims as structured app occurrence rows without applicable permission and separate taxonomic/locality review.

scopeDecision.reason: The atlas supports the preprint name/locality at Sariaya, but neither source maps the bridge to a channel route, and the Quezon profile uses a different spelling while describing a central river basin. No geometry or species-level assertion is supported.

nextActions: Seek a peer-reviewed/publisher or institutional record and item-specific reuse terms for this preprint.

Resolve whether the Quezon profile name MalakingIlog is the same feature as the atlas/preprint Malaquing Ilog through an authorized ecological-profile volume or official Sariaya/Quezon hydrography source; do not merge by spelling or municipality alone.
Seek dated, site-linked vouchers or independent reusable surveys for both rivers; keep local interview reports separate from specimen-confirmed records.
nonClaims: The preprint does not establish current Pterygoplichthys presence or species-level identity in either Sariaya river.
The reported 2003 history is attributed to residents and is not a field collection date.
No whole-river route, watershed, geometry, legal access, fishing status, safety, diet, or bait recommendation is inferred.
